What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell the A natural minor scale.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A, B, C, D, E, F, G, A (no sharps or flats)

What is the step pattern of the natural: Compared with the major scale on the same note, which scale degrees are lowered in natural minor?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The 3rd, 6th and 7th, each by a half step (1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7).

What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell the E natural minor scale.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): E, F#, G, A, B, C, D, E (one sharp)

What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell the D natural minor scale.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): D, E, F, G, A, Bb, C, D (one flat)

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which major key is the relative major of A minor?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): C major. Both have no sharps or flats, and C is a minor 3rd above A.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is the leading tone?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The note a half step below the tonic. It leads up to the tonic (G# in A minor).

What is the step pattern of the natural: How does the harmonic minor scale differ from natural minor?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The 7th note is raised by a half step.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell the A harmonic minor scale.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A, B, C, D, E, F, G#, A

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is the melodic minor scale?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Natural minor with the 6th and 7th raised going up. Coming down, it uses natural minor.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell the A melodic minor scale going up and down.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Up: A, B, C, D, E, F#, G#, A. Down: A, G, F, E, D, C, B, A.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which step in the harmonic minor scale is three half steps wide?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The step from the 6th note to the raised 7th (F to G# in A minor).

What is the step pattern of the natural: Right-hand fingering for the A minor scale going up one octave?
Left-hand fingering for the A minor scale going up one octave?
Which finger plays Bb in the right-hand D minor scale?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Finger 3 (D1 E2 F3 G1 A2 Bb3 C4 D5).

What is the step pattern of the natural: How many flats does the D minor key signature have?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): One flat: Bb.

What is the step pattern of the natural: In D melodic minor going up, which notes are raised?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): B (Bb becomes B natural) and C (becomes C#). Coming down they return to Bb and C.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What does a slash chord such as D/F# mean?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A D chord with F# as the lowest note (the bass).

What is the step pattern of the natural: What does each slash in a chord chart bar stand for?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): One beat.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What does a chord chart sign with a slash and a dot on each side mean?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Play the previous bar again.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What does a thick bar line with two dots mean?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A repeat sign: go back to the repeat sign at the start of the section and play it again.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is a lead sheet?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A melody on a staff with chord symbols above it.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell the G7 chord.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): G, B, D, F

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is the relative minor of a major key?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The minor key that shares its key signature. It starts a minor 3rd below the major tonic, on the 6th note of the major scale.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What are parallel keys?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A major key and a minor key with the same tonic, such as C major and C minor.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is the relative minor of D major, and how many sharps?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): B minor, two sharps (F# and C#).

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is the key signature of C minor?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Three flats: Bb, Eb, Ab.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is the key signature of G minor?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Two flats: Bb and Eb.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is the relative minor of Bb major?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): G minor (two flats).

What is the step pattern of the natural: What are the two methods for playing a lead sheet in this stage?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): 1. Left hand root, right hand triad. 2. Right hand melody, left hand chords.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell the C, G, Am and F triads.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): C: C, E, G. G: G, B, D. Am: A, C, E. F: F, A, C.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell the triads of the G D Em C loop.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): G: G, B, D. D: D, F#, A. Em: E, G, B. C: C, E, G.

What is the step pattern of the natural: In a lead sheet, which hand plays louder when the right hand has the melody?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The right hand (the melody). Play the left-hand chords softer.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What does a capo do?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): It presses all six strings against one fret, so every open string sounds higher by that many half steps.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Where does the capo go relative to the fret wire?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Close behind the fret wire (on the nut side), not on top of it.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which chord sounds when you play a G shape with the capo on fret 2?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A major.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which chord sounds when you play a C shape with the capo on fret 5?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): F major.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Does a capo chart list shapes or sounding chords in this book?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The shapes you play.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which note makes a triad major or minor?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The 3rd: four half steps above the root in a major triad, three in a minor triad.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Spell C major and C minor.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): C major: C, E, G. C minor: C, Eb, G.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is the first step in hearing whether a melody is major or minor?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Find the home note (the tonic), then compare the 3rd above it.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which note changes between A major and A minor?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): C# in A major becomes C in A minor.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which keys are Schumann's Album for the Young, Op. 68, No. 1 (Melody) and No. 2 (Soldiers' March) in?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): No. 1 is in C major and No. 2 is in G major.

What is the step pattern of the natural: How long does a dotted quarter note last?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): 1.5 beats: a quarter plus an eighth.

What is the step pattern of the natural: How do you count a dotted quarter followed by an eighth, starting on beat 1?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): 1 (&) (2) &. The eighth falls on the & of beat 2.

What is the step pattern of the natural: In melody over accompaniment, which part is played louder?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The melody. Keep the accompaniment softer.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What do the letters p i m a stand for?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Picking-hand fingers: p thumb, i index, m middle, a ring.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which strings does the thumb (p) play in this stage?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The bass strings 6, 5 and 4.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Which finger plays string 3, which plays string 2, and which plays string 1?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): i plays string 3, m plays string 2, a plays string 1.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is fingerpicking pattern 1?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): p i m a in quarter notes: the bass note, then strings 3, 2 and 1.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is fingerpicking pattern 2?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): p i m i p i m i in eighth notes.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is a broken chord?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A chord whose notes are played one after another instead of together.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Name the notes of the 1-5-8-5 pattern for a C chord.
Name the notes of the 1-5-10-5 pattern for a C chord.
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): C3, G3, E4, G3 (the 10th is an octave above the 3rd).

What is the step pattern of the natural: What are the 1-5-8 notes for Am?
What are the first steps of the scan before you sight-read in a new key?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Name the key from the key signature, mark the notes it changes, decide major or minor, then scan for accidentals.

What is the step pattern of the natural: In G major, which note does the key signature change?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Every F becomes F#.

What is the step pattern of the natural: In F major, which note does the key signature change?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Every B becomes Bb.

What is the step pattern of the natural: In A minor, which accidental usually appears, and why?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): G#, the raised 7th (the leading tone) that leads up to A.

What is the step pattern of the natural: How long does an accidental last?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Until the end of the bar.

What is the step pattern of the natural: Where does the picking hand rest for palm muting?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The outside edge of the hand rests lightly on the strings near the bridge saddle.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What is a chuck?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): A percussive click made by strumming while the fretting fingers touch the strings but do not press them.

What is the step pattern of the natural: How do you count sixteenth notes?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): 1 e & a, 2 e & a, 3 e & a, 4 e & a

What is the step pattern of the natural: How many sixteenth notes are in one beat of 4/4?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): Four.

What is the step pattern of the natural: What stays constant in sixteenth-note strumming even when the pick misses the strings?
W H W W H W W (whole and half steps): The down-up arm motion, four times per beat.
